figures.title: Title composite
figures.caption: Composite generated from the authoritative ICRS Cell3 basis, all 27 centered nodes, the fixed G_phase matrix, the Earth-CMB translation vector, and the complete 366-epoch Earth response ledger.

figures.title: Authoritative Cell3 frontispiece
figures.caption: Dimensionally correct centered Cell3 in ICRS native coordinates. The twelve edges, six boundary faces, all 27 half-step nodes, integer addresses, primitive vectors, Earth-CMB direction, and transformed translation direction are generated from source arrays. The two cosmic arrows are direction arrows scaled uniformly for legibility.

figures.title: Canonical local Cell3
figures.caption: The same intrinsic Cell3 shape in its canonical local rendering: a lies on x, b lies in the x-y plane, and c completes the oblique cell. Axes retain native length units and all node coordinates are computed by p=(1/2)B L.

figures.title: Exact 27-node address grammar
figures.caption: All 27 centered integer addresses. Mapping L to physical coordinates through p=(1/2)B L preserves the exact finite grammar while introducing the measured oblique metric.

figures.title: Six boundary-plane node panels
figures.caption: Each boundary plane is projected into an orthonormal in-plane coordinate system, so distances are preserved in native units. Every panel contains the complete nine-node half-step array and exact integer labels.

figures.title: Central Cell3 plane families
figures.caption: The three central planes pass through the Cell3 origin and are spanned by the ab, ac, and bc primitive-vector pairs. The arrows are the source unit normals scaled uniformly for display; plane patches retain native dimensions.

figures.title: Direct and reciprocal metrics
figures.caption: Numerical matrices computed from the canonical Cell3 basis. M=B^T B measures squared lengths and angular shear; R=M^-1 reads reciprocal-plane and volume-sensitivity response.

figures.title: Anisotropic G_phase transformation
figures.caption: The sphere has radius |V_E|=369812.502 m/s. Mapping that sphere through G_phase produces an ellipsoid with semiaxes |V_E| times the three eigenvalues. The actual transformed vector has magnitude 930825.217 m/s.

figures.title: Rank-two transverse response disk
figures.caption: For a one-kilogram continuous rim and unit angular speed, the analytic map F/kappa_F=(1/2)n cross(G_phase V_E) sends all directed spin axes on the unit sphere into a closed disk perpendicular to G_phase V_E. The two axes parallel and antiparallel to G_phase V_E map to the disk center.

figures.title: Continuous-rim self-term cancellation
figures.caption: The local R omega^2 C(theta) contribution is radial. Opposite rim points have equal scalar C and opposite radial directions, so the continuous vector integral vanishes. Arrow lengths are uniformly rescaled; rim coordinates are exact metres for R=0.5 m.

figures.title: Constrained-axis continuous-rim force ellipse
figures.caption: The exact 0.1-degree directed-axis sweep. The ellipse semiaxes are 465412.609 and 396230.434 N per (kappa_F rad/s). Its plane is perpendicular to G_phase V_E, and the full-cycle vector mean is zero.

figures.title: Continuous-rim orientation channels
figures.caption: The transverse-to-CMB magnitude is constant, the CMB-parallel component is sinusoidal, and the total magnitude ranges between the two ellipse semiaxes. Reversing the directed axis by 180 degrees reverses the force vector.

figures.title: Calibrated force versus RPM
figures.caption: Linear constitutive scaling for a one-kilogram continuous rim at the maximum-force orientation using kappa_F=3.0740508997e-11. The intersections occur near 6.6746e5 RPM for 1 N and 6.545e6 RPM for 9.80665 N.

figures.title: Earth vector calibration
figures.caption: The observed one-year ICRS eccentricity-vector change is projected onto the computed unit-coupling K response. The fitted vector contains 78.716 percent of the observed vector power; the observed and fitted directions are separated by 27.474 degrees.

figures.title: Independent Earth calibration channels
figures.caption: Full-vector projection and scalar apsidal-rate matching differ by 2.037 percent relative to their mean. The midpoint is retained as the recommended Earth coupling; the channel interval is an internal consistency interval, not a statistical confidence interval.

figures.title: Calibrated annual Earth response
figures.caption: Daily 366-epoch Earth-Sun differential acceleration at kappa_F=3.0740508997e-11. The magnitude spans 5.735920e-10 to 7.157364e-10 m/s^2; variability is generated by changing geometry and velocity relative to the fixed anisotropic tensor.

figures.title: Near-quadrature Earth response
figures.caption: The source daily integration gives a 89.5997-degree lag from maximum positive tangential K forcing to maximum positive orbital-size response. This near-quarter-cycle timing follows the integrated transverse forcing geometry and is not, by itself, evidence of elastic energy storage.

figures.title: Cell3 shear redistribution
figures.caption: Straightening the cell while keeping the three edge lengths fixed preserves trace(M) and the complete 351-pair squared-distance sum. Cell3 has 0.759427 times the rectilinear volume and 1.251733 times the reciprocal trace.
